extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers/engineers/mathematicians implementing Groebner-basis conversions using modwalk.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and examples for SINGULAR library procedures (modrWalk, modfWalk, modWalk) that compute/convert Groebner/standard bases using modular methods. Shows required preconditions, example usage, parameters (radius, ordering, weight vector), and the expected return values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return value (modrWalk / modfWalk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: a standard basis of I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation explicitly states that modrWalk and modfWalk return a standard basis of the input ideal I. Example outputs (J[1], J[2], ...) are shown. For modrWalk the page shows: "Return: a standard basis of I" and for modfWalk the same wording is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation method (modular over Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure computes a standard basis of I (over the rational numbers) by using modular methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This note appears under both modrWalk and modfWalk: the routines use modular techniques to compute the standard basis over the rationals. The examples demonstrate conversion results produced by these modular computations (large rational-coefficient polynomials shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precondition: input must be a Groebner basis for source ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: I is assumed to be a Dp-Groebner basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show workflow: compute I = std(I) in the original ring/ordering, then use fetch to move the ideal into the target ring/variable order and call the modular walk routine. Comments in examples: "// I is assumed to be a Dp-Groebner basis." This indicates the routine expects the input ideal to already be given as a Groebner (standard) basis for the source monomial ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: convert Groebner/standard basis between orderings
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a Groebner/standard basis for a different monomial ordering (e.g., compute a (a(w),lp)-Groebner basis from a Dp-Groebner basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate converting a Dp-Groebner basis to an lp-Groebner basis and also to a (a(w),lp)-Groebner basis: e.g. set intvec w = 3,2,1,2; ring S3 = 0, (c,d,b,a), (a(w),lp); // I is assumed to be a Dp-Groebner basis. We compute a (a(w),lp)-Groebner basis. ideal J = modrWalk(I,"Dp",w); The routines are intended for basis conversion between orderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter: radius (modrWalk example)
rubrics_metrics.description: modrWalk takes an integer 'radius' parameter (example: int radius = 2; ideal J = modrWalk(I,radius);).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example demonstrates supplying a radius parameter to modrWalk; the manual shows "int radius = 2; ideal J = modrWalk(I,radius);" but does not provide a detailed textual definition of radius in this excerpt. It is presented as a required/optional numeric parameter controlling the modular-walk behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: compute std(I), fetch into new ring, then call modular-walk
rubrics_metrics.description: Workflow in examples: compute I = std(I) in source ring; open target ring with desired monomial ordering; use fetch(R1,I) to move the ideal; then call modrWalk/modfWalk (possibly with ordering and weight arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete example sequence from the page: LIB "modwalk.lib"; ring R1 = 0, (x,y,z,t), dp; ideal I = 3x3+x2+1, 11y5+y3+2, 5z4+z2+4; I = std(I); ring R2 = 0, (x,y,z,t), lp; ideal I = fetch(R1, I); int radius = 2; ideal J = modrWalk(I,radius); For other examples: ring S1 = 0, (a,b,c,d), Dp; I = std(I); ring S2 = 0, (c,d,b,a), lp; ideal I = fetch(S1,I); ideal J = modrWalk(I, radius, "Dp"); This demonstrates the intended sequence of operations to perform a basis conversion using the library routines.
